subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In the TCP/IP model, which layer is responsible for routing packets across networks using IP addresses?
options: Application layer
Link layer
Network (Internet) layer
Transport layer
questions.explain: The network/internet layer handles addressing and routing of packets using IP addresses.

questions.q: What happens during packet switching?
options: Packets must always arrive in the order they were sent
Data is split into packets that can travel by different routes and are reassembled
Data is sent as one continuous unbroken stream
A dedicated physical circuit is reserved for the whole transmission
questions.explain: Packet switching splits data into packets that may take different routes and are reassembled at the destination.

questions.q: Which is an environmental concern linked to the rapid replacement of electronic devices?
options: Improved screen resolutions
Faster internet speeds
Greater storage capacity
Growing amounts of electronic waste (e-waste)
questions.explain: Frequently discarding old devices creates large amounts of e-waste that can harm the environment.

questions.q: Which of the following is a benefit of cloud computing?
options: It works perfectly with no internet connection
It removes all concerns about data security
Your data is never stored on remote servers
Files can be accessed from any internet-connected device
questions.explain: A key benefit of the cloud is access to your files and applications from any device with an internet connection.

questions.q: What is the purpose of FTP?
options: Transferring files between computers
Encrypting passwords
Browsing web pages
Resolving domain names
questions.explain: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is used to transfer files between computers.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of social engineering?
options: Pretending to be IT support over the phone to persuade a worker to reveal their password
Flooding a server with automated traffic
Encrypting files with a strong key
Splitting data into packets for transmission
questions.explain: Social engineering manipulates people into giving away information, such as impersonating IT support to obtain a password.

questions.q: What does IoT (Internet of Things) refer to?
options: Everyday objects with sensors and connectivity that exchange data over the internet
A new type of CPU register
A method of compressing video files
A programming language for websites
questions.explain: The IoT is the network of everyday devices fitted with sensors and internet connectivity that collect and share data.

questions.q: Which is a typical advantage of using robots for tasks such as deep-sea or bomb-disposal work?
options: They never need any power source
They always feel fear and act cautiously
They can replace the internet
They can operate in environments too dangerous for humans
questions.explain: Robots can work in hazardous environments, keeping human workers safe from danger.

questions.q: Which is a privacy concern raised by many IoT devices in the home?
options: They make the home network faster
They reduce electricity bills automatically
They may collect personal data that could be misused if not secured
They remove the need for passwords
questions.explain: IoT devices often gather personal data, which raises privacy and security risks if not properly protected.

questions.q: How do an IP address and a MAC address differ?
options: Only MAC addresses are used on the internet
An IP address can change between networks while a MAC address is fixed to the hardware
An IP address is permanent while a MAC address changes each session
They are two names for exactly the same thing
questions.explain: An IP address can change depending on the network, whereas a MAC address is fixed to the device's hardware.

questions.q: What best describes machine learning?
options: A method of compressing images without loss
A computer following a fixed set of rules written by a programmer
Systems that improve their performance on a task by learning from data
A way of storing files on optical discs
questions.explain: Machine learning enables systems to improve at a task by finding patterns in data rather than being explicitly programmed with every rule.

questions.q: What does the bandwidth of a network refer to?
options: The physical length of the cabling
The number of devices connected
The amount of data that can be transmitted in a given time
The distance between two routers
questions.explain: Bandwidth is the amount of data that can be transmitted in a given time.

questions.q: Which statement about a peer-to-peer network is correct?
options: A central server controls all the data
All computers have equal status and can share resources directly
Clients cannot share files with one another
It always requires specialist server software
questions.explain: In peer-to-peer networks all computers have equal status and share resources directly.

questions.q: In a star network topology, how are devices connected?
options: Devices are connected in a single closed loop
Devices share a single backbone cable
Each device connects directly to every other device
Every device connects to a central switch or hub
questions.explain: In a star topology every device connects to a central switch or hub.

questions.q: A company stores its software and data on remote servers accessed over the internet instead of local machines. This is best described as:
options: Run-length encoding
Cloud computing
Virtual memory
An embedded system
questions.explain: Using remote internet-accessed servers for storage and software is cloud computing.

questions.q: On the web, what is the role of a web server?
options: It only displays web pages on the user's screen
It stores website files and sends pages to browsers that request them
It translates IP addresses into domain names exclusively
It physically connects two computers with a cable
questions.explain: A web server stores the files of a website and serves the requested pages back to the user's browser.

questions.q: What is a typical advantage of using robots in a car manufacturing factory?
options: They never require any maintenance
They are always cheaper than humans in every situation
They can work continuously with high precision and consistency
They can show empathy to customers
questions.explain: Robots can repeat tasks consistently and precisely for long periods without tiring.

questions.q: Why is human oversight often recommended when AI systems make important decisions?
options: AI only works without electricity
AI can make mistakes or reflect bias in its training data
AI always refuses to make any decision
Humans cannot understand any AI output
questions.explain: AI can produce errors or biased outcomes, so human oversight helps catch and correct unfair or wrong decisions.

questions.q: Which is a potential negative social impact of automation replacing manual jobs?
options: More consistent product quality
Increased unemployment in some sectors
Faster production speeds
Lower running costs for businesses
questions.explain: Automation can displace human workers, leading to job losses in some industries.

questions.q: Which scenario best illustrates the IoT improving efficiency in agriculture?
options: Manually watering every field by hand
Storing crop records on an optical disc
A farmer reading a printed weather forecast
Soil sensors automatically signalling irrigation systems when crops need water
questions.explain: Networked sensors automatically triggering irrigation based on real-time data is an IoT application improving efficiency.

questions.q: What is a common drawback of relying heavily on automated decision-making systems?
options: They always run without electricity
It can be hard to know how or why a decision was reached
They make storage non-volatile
They never need any data
questions.explain: Automated systems can be opaque, making it difficult to explain or challenge how a decision was made.

questions.q: In a client-server network, what does the server typically do?
options: Provides shared resources and services to clients
Cannot control access to files
Relies on each client to store all the data
Has equal status with every other computer
questions.explain: In client-server, the server provides centralised resources and services to clients.
